articles.summary: Developers invited to explore emotion, voice and movement using the Arduino UNO R4 WiFi powered by the Renesas RA4M1 microcontroller PHOENIX – Hackster, an Avnet community, has launched Emotion in Motion, a robotics design challenge inviting developers, engineers, makers and students to create projects exploring emotion, voice and motor control. Hackster is giving away 500 Arduino® UNO R4 WiFi boards, powered by the Renesas RA4M1 microcontroller, to help participants bring their ideas to life. Emotion in Motion challenges participants to explore the more human side of robotics and electronics. Projects can mimic or respond to emotions, interact through voice, demonstrate fine motor skills and dexterity, play and react, or help people complete tasks. “Robotics isn't only about what a machine can do, but increasingly how naturally people can interact with it,” said Dianne Kibbey, Senior Director, Community Strategy and Hackster.io at Avnet. “Emotion in Motion challenges our
articles.title: Hackster launches Emotion in Motion robotics design challenge with Renesas and Arduino

articles.summary: Global engineering community invited to design and build innovative robotics projects element14 , an Avnet Community, has launched the Rise of the Robots design challenge, inviting engineers, makers and technology enthusiasts to design and build innovative robotics projects using a kit of development hardware, motors and sensors. Ten selected challengers will receive a free kit of components to support the design and build of their projects. Participants can explore a wide range of robotics applications, including hospitality, delivery, disaster response, industrial and companion robots. Participants will document their build process through forum updates and a project blog, with entries evaluated based on innovation, technical merit and creative use of the provided components.
